Il Napoli di Massimiliano Allegri torna alla vittoria, battendo in una partita sofferta il Torino di Ignazio Abate e mettendo maggiormente al sicuro la posizione dell'allenatore livornese.

Dopo un primo tempo combattuto e tosto, gli azzurri spaccano la partita nella ripresa soprattutto per merito di Lang, che prima impegna Perri e poi serve a McTominay l'assist per il gol decisivo del centrocampista scozzese, abile a battere il portiere avversario con un destro all'angolino.

A nulla vale l'assedio finale del Toro che, anzi, nell'ultima azione della partita rischia anche di subire il secondo gol proprio con Lang lanciato a rete, sul cui tiro però è bravo Perri a evitare il 2-0. Con questa vittoria, il Napoli va momentaneamente all'ottavo posto in classifica a quota 15 punti.

#84600. Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4854 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.
  • This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.
  • In a recent development, he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

In a recent development, he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

According to recent reports, given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

According to recent reports, that was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a new manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

Recent findings suggest that the victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

Playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

In a recent development, there were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

In a recent development, millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

According to recent reports, millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

According to recent reports, newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

In a recent development, so much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

According to recent reports, well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil said: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

Sources indicate that “We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

Industry observers note that as for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

The draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

It has been revealed that the third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:.

Crystal Palace 3-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-3 Bradford City.

From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

“I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” stated Willock after the match.

“100% [the competition is vital], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a new coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a significant game in keeping that momentum.”.

"We mentioned at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT.

Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:.

Industry observers note that moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

Seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

Willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

Sources indicate that newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

Finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

You can hear the travelling fans now!

Marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

Issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

Millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

Recent findings suggest that double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

Free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

It has been revealed that what colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

Industry observers note that it’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

According to recent reports, newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

Industry observers note that scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Promising restart for the home side.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:.

Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here.

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

According to recent reports, millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

Recent findings suggest that the game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

Industry observers note that the delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

González is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

Millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

According to recent reports, hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

It has been revealed that I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

First piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

Barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

Industry observers note that wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

In a recent development, newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

Industry observers note that another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

Again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

Sources indicate that murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

Newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

In a recent development, fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Just a reminder of the teams starting today:.

Starting XI: Filip Marschall; Jordi Osei-Tutu, Caleb Taylor, Jake Cooper, Elkan Baggott; Lyndon Dykes, Jenson Metcalfe; Camiel Neghli, Daniel Kelly, Romain Esse; Zak Lovelace.

Substitutes: Regan Monty, Tristan Parkes, Sacha Vieira, George Beaumont, Yanis Issoufou, George Evans, Taïryk Arconte, Alfie Massey, Zak Sturge.

Starting XI: Lukás Hornícek; Lewis Hall, Fabian Schär, Amar Dedic, Sven Botman; Jacob Murphy, Nico González; Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Joe Willock; Yoane Wissa.

Substitutes: Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga, Malick Thiaw, Nick Pope, Lewis Miley, Bazoumana Touré, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Aladji Bamba, Sean Steur.

In a recent development, the teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

"We've tried to find the right balance" ⚖️Matthias Jaissle on his team selection for tonight's match with Millwall ⚫️ pic.twitter.com/kiRRxAgLk8.

We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

Industry observers note that alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach says has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

Sources indicate that at the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.

You can read Luke Edwards’ full story on that here.

It has been revealed that the Premier League teams playing in European competitions enter the EFL Cup in this round, with all 16 fixtures being played over five match days. As well as tonight’s games there will be:.

Peterborough United vs Barnsley (7.45pm).

Fleetwood Town vs Sheffield United (7.45pm).

Manchester City vs Norwich City (7.30pm).

*all kick-off at 8pm, unless stated otherwise.

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

Jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

Bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

Industry observers note that aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight fresh signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

The visitors have arrived in south London.

We've made it to South East London 👋 pic.twitter.com/nh8Fpa37xT.

We’re bringing you the action from the pick of tonight’s EFL Cup games but there are also four games kicking off at 7.45pm:.

Crystal Palace vs Middlesbrough.

The Champions League also returns tonight and you can follow along with both our blogs:.

Aston Villa are presently 3-1 up against Club Brugge in Belgium – follow the action here.

Manchester City will face Porto at 8.00pm – our live blog has just gone live here with the team news from both sides.

Here is how the visitors are lining up:.

Yoane Wissa takes the captain’s armband tonight, while Jacob Ramsey starts up front after scoring a late equaliser against Bournemouth on Saturday.

Your Mags at Millwall ✊ pic.twitter.com/zfnHgTlWgh.

Here is your Millwall starting XI:.

Keeper Filip Marschall is making his debut while Jensen Metcalfe is back in the squad after his red card against Bolton was overturned on appeal.

How your Lions line-up tonight 🔢 pic.twitter.com/wEp6qLIz4Y.

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

In a recent development, newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the upcoming season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

I primi 15 minuti di oggi non sono andati benissimo, dopo molto meglio, abbiamo sofferto un po' sui nostri calci piazzati a favore. Eravamo un po' piantati sulle seconde palle. Era da un po' di tempo che sbagliavamo sempre i secondi tempi, a questo giro siamo stati sul pezzo e li abbiamo messi in grandissima difficoltà.

Industry observers note that gattuso avrà un merito su quel che sta facendo la Lazio? Per come lavorano in allenamento. Ieri ero tranquillo, oggi abbiamo messo in campo Diogo, Pedraza,. La tranquillità me la danno i dati, il senso di appartenenza. Mi prendo questo merito: aver fatto diventare in pochissimo tempo questa squadra una famiglia.

Sources indicate that io ho giocato con otto palloni d'oro nella mia carriera. Taylor vede cose che gli altri non vedono. Gli altri avrebbero tirato di piattone, io sinceramente già lo stavo mandando a quel paese. Nel mio modo di pensare il calcio, quella giocata non m'è passata neanche per l'anticamera del cervello. Dico Rui Costa, dai.

Frattesi? Io non ho salvato la vita a nessuno. Lui è un capoccione, esagera sempre. Ha bisogno d'affetto, come tanti giocatori. Ha bisogno anche di prendere le mazzate nei denti, vuol giocare come dice lui. Il merito su quel che sta facendo è suo. Sono contento che abbia fatto gol di sinistro. Sono contento di tutti, sono felice di allenarli. Oggi mi dispiace che Dele abbia fatto 11 minuti, meriterebbe molto di più. Tanti altri meriterebbero di fare qualche minuto in più, si allenano in un modo incredibile.

Recent findings suggest that isaksen? Dentro non si passava oggi, dovevamo andare in verticale. L'abbiamo fatto pochissime volte, e quelle poche volte siamo rusciti a mettere pensiero. Ha fatto una partita incredibile anche con la Danimarca.

Supercoppa? Per me è un regalo, io non c'entro nulla. Non è un impiccio, anzi. È una coppa. Manca un mese, pensa se possiamo pensare alla coppa. Quando arriverà, ci penseremo. Stai lì, provi a giocartela, giochi contro una squadra che sta dettando legge. Adesso recuperiamo due giorni e poi da martedì iniziano a preparare la sfida contro il Torino.

It has been revealed that qual è il segreto di questa Lazio? Noi proponiamo, però chi propone deve avere dall'altra parte gente che ci crede fortemente. Quando il giocatore la pensa in maniera diversa, lì viene il difficile. Bisogna esser bravi a fargli capire perché vogliamo fare determinate cose. Siamo stati bravi noi, sono bravi loro quando facciamo i lavori individuali. Con tutta questa organizzazione che abbiamo messo giù, loro si trovano bene. Noi proponiamo e per il momento tutto sta andando bene. La base di tutto è il lavoro: se vuoi giocare in questo modo qui, la fatica ti deve rimanere nella testa. A parlare è facile, non basta.

L’allenatore del Napoli Massimiliano Allegri ha parlato in conferenza stampa nel post-partita di Napoli-Torino. Ecco quanto sottolineato da IamNaples.it.

According to recent reports, “Vergara si è fatto male, non so per quanto tempo, l’anno scorso era una novità, ha un dispendio di energie mentali diverso, questi infortuni arrivano anche per questo motivo. I ragazzi sono stati bravi soprattutto a mettersi al pari del Torino per intensità, mi è piaciuta anche l’attenzione sui calci piazzati e in certi momenti della partita, prendevamo gol da otto partite, è stato importante non prenderlo. De Bruyne? Bisogna essere realisti, martedì abbiamo una partita bella da giocare ma, guardando il calendario, abbiamo sempre pensato che ci giocassimo il passaggio del turno nelle ultime tre partite. Noa Lang è stato bravo, non solo ha fatto l’assist ma ha anche recuperato il pallone da cui nasce il gol. Il calcio di Allegri non esiste, esiste il calcio proposto dal Napoli che deve recuperare qualche giocatore in più. In queste sedici partite, tranne che a Genova dove abbiamo fatto un primo tempo brutto ma nel secondo abbiamo fatto bene, abbiamo concesso dei gol agli avversari in maniera troppo facile”.

Gary Neville rolls out surprise defence of Diogo Dalot and names the THREE defenders Mauricio Pochettino should sell before Man United boo boy

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1194 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.
  • The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026.

Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.

The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.

But as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford, Neville urged the latest manager not to immediately expel the defender, despite his drop-off in form.

Industry observers note that 'I think if he was in a decent back four he'd be alright,' Neville told Stick to United co-host Mark Goldbridge on Tuesday. 'But he's got a shocking back four alongside him.

'Positionally he's not great. He could be better on the ball. He could be better at everything he does. Of course he could. I just think he's such an easy target, Dalot. I honestly do.'.

Neville admitted that sometimes he listens to his fellow Man United-supporting friends deriding Dalot and wonders 'are they watching something that I don't see?'.

Gary Neville has defended Man United star Diogo Dalot - arguing that he has team-mates who are far weaker.

The Portugal international has come in for heavy criticism from supporters this season.

But in his opinion, there are three defenders that he would let go in the 'first wave' of changes in Manchester.

'I'd be getting (Noussair) Mazraoui well gone before him,' he continued. 'I'd be getting (Lisandro) Martinez gone well before him. I'll be getting (Matthijs) De Ligt gone well before him.

Sources indicate that '(De Ligt has) got one big problem. He doesn’t play football. If a player is injury prone and doesn't play football, just because he hasn't played doesn't mean to say that he should go above a player who's played every single week and he's throwing his hand up. You want someone who's actually reliable and play. De Ligt has to go. De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui.'.

Another stalwart in the team that Neville was keen to have a second chance under Pochettino was Luke Shaw.

'He will keep Shaw because he knows him and he'll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries,' he added. 'So he'll have to manage him. So he'll have to bring a left back in. But let's just say who he'll keep.

'He'll keep Shaw. He'll keep (Harry) Maguire because he'll trust him and he'll think that he's basically a soldier and someone who can do a job for him.

'He'll keep (Leny) Yoro because I think he'll think "I've got something there that I can work with". (But) I think he's a little bit gangly, all over the place right now. And he looks like he's going to slip every time. He's got that sort of Bambi-on-ice (look).

'Physically what will happen is with Yoro, he'll go one way or the other. I like the fact he's been brought into the French team. It tells me sometimes you just have got to connect the dots and think, "okay, well, if they think he's good, then we must be missing something here because we're not seeing it yet, are we?".'.

Neville went on to suggest that Yoro was lacking the connection within his body that Premier League rivals such as Jeremy Jacquet are already able to harness – something Sir Alex Ferguson had identified in Rio Ferdinand when he was at West Ham.

Like Ferdinand, Neville backed Yoro to flourish as he taps into that connection and improves his strength and stability.

'So Yoro he will keep: Yoro, Maguire and Shaw I think he'll keep and I think he'll keep Dalot. To start with,' Neville mentioned. 'He'll have to bring in three defenders to go above them. Let's be clear. He'll have to bring in three defenders.

'Mazraoui I would lose, De Ligt I would lose because he's injury prone. Martinez 100 per cent. 100 per cent. 100 per cent.'.

As well as struggling for form this season, Martinez has been a challenging presence in the Man United squad this term, boldly calling out the Man United hierarchy during a firebrand interview last month.

Neville was more interested in latest head coach Mauricio Pochettino despatching Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt.

Lisandro Martinez has been an unsettled presence in the side this season and hit out at the club's recruiting last month.

The Argentina star implied that he was disappointed with the club's recruitment strategy over the summer, and was forced to hold clear-the-air talks to smooth his return to the side.

Neville added that he would send Ayden Heaven on loan to get experience in the lower divisions to 'build' his ability up, as it was borderline 'unfair' to be 'putting him in' the side at present.

But not all of the changes can come quickly for Pochettino, who has little time before taking charge of Man United against Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.

In a recent development, 'First wave, end of the season,' Neville clarified of what he believes Pochettino's blueprint for change will be. 'No, he can't get rid of (them all) in January.

'He has to bring one or two defenders in January if he can. But he can't get rid of all those in his first wave. He's only got one month till January.'.

The drawn-out process of sacking Carrick began last week when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada flew to Monaco for talks with co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer ownership group.

While his future was on the chopping block, Carrick held training sessions at Carrington before the axe finally swung last Thursday.

Pochettino was appointed days later and gave a tearful farewell press conference ahead of his penultimate game with the United States national team on Saturday.

Sources indicate that ‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he told the press. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

Si avvicina la ripresa del campionato dopo la sosta per le Nazionali, e l'Inter si prepara ad affrontare la trasferta di Bergamo contro l'Atalanta, valida per la 12ª giornata di Serie A. I nerazzurri, secondi in classifica a quota 28 punti, sono reduci dalla vittoria di San Siro contro il Como nell'ultimo impegno prima della pausa, mentre la squadra di Sarri ha conquistato tre punti in casa del Monza nell'ultimo turno e occupa la dodicesima posizione in classifica con 14 punti.

Sono 130 i precedenti tra Inter e Atalanta in Serie A: i meneghini contano 71 successi contro i 24 dei bergamaschi, con 35 pareggi a completare il quadro. L'Inter è la squadra contro cui l'Atalanta ha perso più partite (71) e ha subito più gol (234) nella massima serie. L'Inter è reduce da una serie positiva contro la Dea, avendo collezionato sette vittorie e un pareggio nelle ultime otto sfide di Serie A, dopo aver raccolto due successi nelle nove precedenti sfide nella competizione (6N, 1P). Per quanto riguarda i precedenti a Bergamo, l'Inter ha conquistato quattro vittorie negli ultimi quattro confronti: sono 25 i successi meneghini in casa della Dea, con 25 pareggi e 15 vittorie dell'Atalanta a completare il bilancio.

It has been revealed that L'Inter ha iniziato il campionato con 9 vittorie nelle prime 11 giornate, realizzando 28 reti e subendone 13. I nerazzurri hanno sempre cercato di imporre il proprio gioco contro ogni avversario affrontato, come testimoniano i dati sul possesso palla (60,7% a partita, secondo miglior dato del campionato) e quelli sulle conclusioni tentate e subite: l’Inter è infatti la squadra che ha effettuato più tiri (234) e che ne ha concessi meno (108) nella Serie A in corso. La differenza tra tiri fatti e subiti è di +126: solo Barcellona (+154) e Bayern Monaco (+127) ne hanno una più ampia nei cinque grandi campionati europei 2026/27.

La squadra di Chivu è anche quella col maggior numero di legni colpiti (10), quella con più palloni toccati (452) in area avversaria e quella che ha realizzato più reti da palla inattiva (8). I nerazzurri hanno dimostrato carattere e voglia di vincere in ogni occasione in questo avvio di stagione, riuscendo quasi sempre a ribaltare uno svantaggio iniziale nei finali di partita: i 13 punti ottenuti dall’Inter da situazioni di svantaggio in questa Serie A sono un record considerando i cinque grandi campionati europei 2026/27. Punti arrivati grazie alla lucidità e alle qualità espresse negli ultimi minuti di partita: quella di Chivu è la squadra che ha ottenuto più punti con gol segnati dopo il 75° minuto di gioco in questa Serie A (nove, più del del doppio rispetto a ogni altra).

Se le proprietà lasciano i dirigenti italiani è un discorso, se invece cambi tutto come ha fatto il Milan oppure la Juventus dopo l'addio di Agnelli, si fa confusione. Sono legato all'identità nazionale, se sono un tifoso di una squadra come il Milan, dove sono tutti stranieri, come faccio a identificarmi in una squadra del genere?".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Departed Leyton Orient favourite Dom Ballard notched 23 goals in 40 appearances as he deservedly picked up the League One Player of the Season award – even more impressive given Richie Wellens’ side only narrowly avoided the drop.

Ballard was the driving force behind avoiding relegation to League Two. The influential striker signed for Bristol City after just one season in East London, but his replacement is filling the void impressively.

Fresh from a superb campaign which yielded 24 goals in all competitions, Kabia flourished at Grimsby Town after arriving from non-league Truro City in the summer of 2025.

His arrival at Brisbane Road was initially met with scepticism following a slow start. But, patience in the 26-year-old frontman has paid off, netting on five occasions and registering three assists in the league.

Kabia’s rise to prominence has been a gradual one, with a prolific campaign at Truro City during the 2024/25 season finally kickstarting his career after spells in Scotland and Ireland.

He wasn’t expected to be an instant hit when he signed for Grimsby Town last summer as he made the two-division jump, but the Irish-born striker soon established himself as the go-to man up top.

Netting crucial goals in their run to the play-off semi-finals, Kabia’s explosive pace in behind and work out of possession for David Artell’s side made him a constant handful with his composure in front of goal another string to his bow.

Leyton Orient meanwhile were enduring a tough campaign, with Ballard one of their only shining lights as they survived relegation by the skin of their teeth. A big-money move felt inevitable after his prolific campaign in a struggling side, and Kabia was swiftly sounded out as an ideal replacement.

In a recent development, given Ballard’s exploits last term, it was hoped Kabia would hit the ground running. But, a solitary goal in his first six appearances made him an early target for scrutiny. Four goals in as many matches at the turn of September turned doubters into believers, but it is his off-the-ball stats which have been particularly eye-catching.

Averaging 33 defensive contributions and 16 tackles per 90 (FotMob), Kabia ranks as one of the best strikers in the third tier for his defensive work which is mandatory in Richie Wellens’ defensively oriented system.

Leyton Orient were never going to be able to attract a player of Ballard’s calibre to replace him, but Kabia brings bags of potential and gives the O’s a different dimension.

His predecessor was more of a poacher who was always in the right place at the right time, while Kabia is more direct and thrives by making runs in behind and using his stature to dominate aerially.

Wellens has also experimented with Kabia in a deeper, attacking midfield position but he has particularly thrived when the O’s have deployed three at the back with creative presences playing directly behind him.

According to recent reports, ultimately though, Kabia will be judged come the end of the season by his goal-scoring return. He may not be close to equaling Ballard’s remarkable return yet with six goals and three assists in 18 games across all competitions, his influence extends far beyond finding the back of the net.

#84587. The curious case of Sebastien Pocognoli looks certain to have a grisly ending... the SFA have hired a dud

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1412 w)

The curious case of Sebastien Pocognoli looks certain to have a grisly ending... the SFA have hired a dud

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1412 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 14:13 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:26 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Of all the many stories written by F Scott Fitzgerald, one of the finest authors and wordsmiths of his time, The Great Gatsby will forever remain his masterpiece.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:13 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:26 EST, 17 November 2026.

Of all the many stories written by F Scott Fitzgerald, one of the finest authors and wordsmiths of his time, The Great Gatsby will forever remain his masterpiece.

In some of his other work written as he travelled across Europe, Fitzgerald also had a line about Switzerland, describing it as a ‘country where very few things begin, but many things end.’.

According to recent reports, it is a curious quote and, like much of Fitzgerald’s work, is open to interpretation. As the man who also wrote The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, curiosity was a common theme.

As for the Curious Case of Sebastien Pocognoli, Switzerland may, indeed, be the country where everything came to an end.

Recent findings suggest that what unfolded in St Gallen on Monday evening was a horror show. Scotland were battered 4-0 by Switzerland’s B team. There is no way to sugar-coat a result like that, no way to dress it up as anything other than an embarrassment. They played OK for half an hour and then fell apart.

Pocognoli claimed afterwards that there were positives to be taken and how some of Scotland’s football was the best they have produced across his six matches in charge.

Sebastien Pocognoli is facing serious questions after a miserable Nations League campaign.

Utter nonsense. That was a manager clutching at straws at the end of a Nations League campaign which has been an unmitigated disaster pretty much from start to finish.

Let’s go back to the very start here. After Steve Clarke had pushed the Scottish Football Association (SFA) into awarding him a latest four-year contract, only to then walk away after the World Cup, it was a chance for a fresh start.

On the day when Pocognoli was unveiled as the newly introduced head coach in August, Ian Maxwell and Craig Mulholland, the SFA’s chief executive and chief football officer, were beaming with positivity.

They told us all how data and AI had been used in the recruitment process, and how several clubs across Europe had been chasing Pocognoli.

They clearly viewed it as a coup to have landed the 39-year-old Belgian, who had won a league title in his homeland with Union Saint-Gilloise before a short stint with Monaco.

Sources indicate that what would the data say now? Six games played, two wins, a draw and three defeats, five goals scored and ten conceded, seven points and a lousy third-placed finish in Group B1.

Both of those wins came against a North Macedonian side who lost all six of their games. They were a pub team – and Scotland still struggled to beat them at Hampden last Friday night.

Pocognoli was unable to inspire any resistance as his side succumbed to defeat in St Gallen.

In a recent development, scotland lost 7-0 on aggregate to Switzerland over the two games. Against Slovenia, a 0-0 draw on the opening day in Ljubljana was then followed with a woeful 2-1 defeat at Hampden.

All of which begs a very simple question. Where, exactly, are the grounds for optimism here? How is this getting any better?

When Pocognoli arrived, he spoke about trying to change the style of play, get Scotland playing a more exciting brand of football, whilst bringing through a newly introduced generation of players.

According to recent reports, it was not a rebuild. He inherited a group of players who were accustomed to success under Clarke and who qualified for three tournaments out of a possible four.

Industry observers note that his remit was to help Scotland take the next step in major tournaments. With a more dynamic style of play, the job was to help the nation take the next step.

There has been no revolution thus far. No evidence whatsoever that this coach is capable of delivering results nor a better style of play.

There is no satisfaction to be taken in any of this. When Pocognoli was appointed, it was, in the eyes of this observer, an interesting and progressive move.

SFA chiefs Craig Mulholland and Ian Maxwell proudly unveil newly introduced boss Pocognoli at Hampden.

Over the past 48 hours or so, there has been a lot of revisionism from some folk about Clarke. ‘Aye, the grass isn’t always greener...’.

In a recent development, that’s garbage. Clarke’s time was up with Scotland. He should never have been handed a latest four-year deal in the first place. At least he did the right thing in resigning after the World Cup.

The whole thing was finished. The problem is that the SFA look like they have appointed a total dud as his successor. Both of those things can be true at the same time.

It is also worth remembering that the only reason we arrived at Pocognoli is because Clarke walked away. The SFA did not instigate any change.

The hiring of a newly introduced head coach was not a proactive change of direction, but a reactive move from an executive body who became accepting of Clarke’s limitations and allowed him to position them over a barrel.

Listen, there is nothing inherently wrong with using data and metrics in football. It’s the modern way. Using data to inform decisions and recruitment processes is smart business.

But the data in itself is no guarantee of success. There are some intangibles in football, things which are harder to quantify. Like a manager who blindly sticks to a system which is patently ill-suited to the players at his disposal.

In a recent development, things like leadership and communication skills. We can cut Pocognoli some slack in that English is not his first language. He comes across as a thoroughly decent and likeable chap. He’s doing his best. He wants to embrace the culture and makes an effort to sing the National Anthem.

Scotland's defeat arose from individual mistakes, a common theme during the Belgian's reign.

All of that is undoubtedly to be welcomed. Good on him. But would anyone describe him as an inspirational figure?

When you listen to him speak, have you ever felt slightly confused in terms of the message he’s actually trying to get across?

In a recent development, how must that sound in the dressing room? When Andy Robertson spoke post-match on Monday night, there was frustration in his voice.

The captain insisted there is simply no time or patience with these things. Scotland need to deliver results now.

To be fair, there actually would be a degree of patience shown by the Tartan Army towards Pocognoli if there was something to actually believe in.

Recent findings suggest that there was a lot of goodwill towards him at the start. If there were signs across these last six games that he could deliver a more exciting team to watch, they would show patience.

Industry observers note that but on the basis of what we’ve seen so far, there’s been absolutely nothing to suggest he can move this team forward. Ask yourself a very simple question – do Scotland pass the eye test?

Are we seeing a team who are playing on the front foot and creating chances? The answer, obviously, is no.

Sources indicate that steve Clarke celebrates Scotland's win over Denmark a year ago... how fans miss such highs.

Many Scotland fans are now confronting the possibility that we might not even qualify for Euro 2028, a tournament which we are co-hosting.

By finishing third in the Nations League, we will now be in pot three for the Euro qualifiers and will face a more difficult group.

Beyond that, we would be relying on the back-door method of one of the best-placed home nations not to qualify directly.

According to recent reports, those Euro qualifiers will start in March of next year. Does Pocognoli even make it that far? Or should the SFA hold their hands up, admit they’ve made a mistake, and rectify it?

In a recent development, that feels unlikely. But on the basis of what we have seen over these first six games, it’s hard to see how this gets any better.

Industry observers note that we are worse now than we were at the end under Clarke. Much, much worse. This is not teething problems. It’s a team who have regressed massively under a head coach who was supposed to move the whole thing forward.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

Sources indicate that so much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

Recent findings suggest that they can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

In a recent development, there is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

Recent findings suggest that they wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Sources indicate that bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

It has been revealed that “In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This shows how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he demonstrated why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

According to recent reports, city had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Recent findings suggest that man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

It has been revealed that “It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland mentioned. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the substantial stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

For Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”.

He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”.

“Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

It has been revealed that “He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”.

It has been revealed that the final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

According to recent reports, enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

Sources indicate that it has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

In a recent development, enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. That is a significant chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

Manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

Donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Recent findings suggest that manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

Recent findings suggest that “It is a hard place to come [Porto],” noted Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that demonstrates a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

Industry observers note that porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the significant favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

23.20 - Inizia la conferenza stampa.

Come sta Vergara? "Si è fatto male, non so per quanto lo perderemo. Dispiace molto, era molto abbattuto. Credo sia stato un infortunio per il periodo, quest'anno ha responsabilità diverse, la Nazionale, maggiori pressioni mentali... Questi infortuni a volte sono causati anche da queste cose". Sulla partita "I ragazzi sono stati molto bravi, hanno avuto l'umiltà e il rispetto di mettersi al pari del Torino. La squadra si è comportata bene anche nelle fasi finali della partita, sui calci d'angolo. Ci dà più solidità non prendere gol stasera, erano 8 partite che subivamo gol".

Ora c'è il Manchester City. "È una partita molto importante e bella da giocare. Bisogna essere realisti: la Champions ce la giocheremo contro Bruges, Sabah e Viking. Quella che dovevamo vincere era contro il Bodo e l'abbiamo fatto. Martedì sarà molto importante e difficile, ma dobbiamo sistemare il campionato. E poi sarà importantissima con il Bruges in casa".

L'ingresso di Lang? "È stato decisivo. Ha fatto l'assist recuperando la palla. Sta crescendo, sono molto contento di lui come di tutti gli altri. Nel primo tempo ho preferito far giocare Spinazzola, che rientrava dall'infortunio, così se fosse successo qualcosa avrei avuto il cambio".

In a recent development, quando si vedrà il calcio di Allegri? "Il calcio di Allegri non esiste. Esiste il calcio fatto di una squadra che è il Napoli, dove dobbiamo recuperare dei giocatori. In queste 10 partite, a parte un paio come il primo tempo contro il Genoa, abbiamo preso troppi gol in maniera facile. Stasera a parte il tiro da fuori area non abbiamo preso tiri, abbiamo difeso meglio dentro il campo dove entravano facilmente. E poi bisogna capire che le partite durano 95 minuti e serve sofferenza, non si può vincere sempre 3-0 senza che gli avversari tirino".

23.25 - Termina la conferenza stampa.

  • It has been revealed that the 23-year-old is in the fourth loan of his career.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Millwall were a lot more selective in who was sent out on loan this campaign after failing to reap the rewards from the players who had spells away from The Den last season. The Lions sanctioned season-long exits for Ra’ees Bangura-Williams, Rafiq Lamptey, Ajay Matthews and Kamarl Grant.

It is the latter who is under greater pressure to succeed in his stint away from the South London outfit, despite signing a contract extension in 2025. Grant was loaned to Bromley in the summer to make it his third spell at the Ravens.

It has been revealed that the 23-year-old is in the fourth loan of his career. He is also yet to feature in the Championship for Millwall. Time is running out for him to prove himself to Alex Neil, and the defender has a tough task to do so in League One.

According to recent reports, grant has been a part of one of the worst defences in the third tier this campaign. The Ravens are averaging 2.54 goals conceded per game as they navigate their first season in League One.

Karl Robinson’s side have an xG against of 1.98. Although the 23-year-old has featured in 11 of their 13 games this term, the blame can’t entirely be put on him. The defender has made 46 recoveries for Bromley and blocked 10 shots.

According to recent reports, grant’s best display this campaign came against league leaders Huddersfield Town during a 2-1 victory. He made 11 defensive contributions and won 100% of his ground duels. The Millwall academy graduate also made seven clearances and wasn’t dribbled past during the 90 minutes.

The Lions will be encouraged by that performance, in particular, given the Terriers’ quality. It does show that despite Bromley’s overall disappointment, the 23-year-old is standing out.

Sources indicate that with Grant having mixed success on loan at Bromley, Millwall’s decision regarding his future will be far from made up. One thing that points to the 23-year-old still having a chance to break through for Neil’s side is their lack of depth at centre-back.

Industry observers note that jake Cooper is in his final year of his contract and Danny Batth likely won’t be kept on for another campaign. Elkan Baggott and Caleb Taylor are the only other senior options, with the latter certain to take up one of the spots next season.

According to recent reports, if Grant can help lower Bromley’s leaky record at the back, then he has every chance of playing a part for Millwall next term. That being said, should an offer come in for the 23-year-old next summer, the Lions would likely entertain a deal.

The South London outfit agreed to Adam Mayor’s permanent exit after he struggled to get into the first team, and the defender is in a similar boat. This season will be telling as to whether the Lions’ academy graduate has a future at The Den or not.
